findings.summary: SURVIVING MUTATION, MEASURED: `refusedForAnotherPod++` -> `refusedForAnotherPod = 1` passes all 501 sequencer tests, the 1,000-seed sweep included. The third counter is the one this commit did NOT give a two-window fixture, and its cross-window unit is unconstrained.
findings.detail: All four claimed sole-killer relationships were RE-MEASURED on this tree and all four hold exactly. Baseline 501/0. (1) `continue;` -> `break;` in the kind guard: 1 red, `aPARTITIONRefusalAFTERANonPartitionFaultIsSTILLCounted`, nothing else. (2) delete the `break` after `refusedForAnotherPod++`: 1 red, `TWORefusalsBLAMINGANOTHERPODCountTheWINDOWOnce`, nothing else. (3) `int writesBefore = 0`: 1 red, `aSECONDWindowIsNotCreditedForTheFIRSTSWrite`, nothing else -- the sweep stays green, as the row records. (4) `int before = 0` and (5) `refusalsSeen = 0` at the top of `observe`: each 2 red, `refusalsACCUMULATEAcrossWindowsAndAreNotRECOUNTED` plus `CommitProtocolSweepTest.theInvariantsHoldAcrossEverySeed`, nothing else. The compound claim in `aSECONDWindowIsNotCreditedForTheFIRSTSWrite`'s javadoc was also re-measured in both directions and is exactly right: `LocalSequencer.java:576` `leases.release()` -> `store.stat(leases.key())` alone reds the sweep on the gracefulReleases floor (0 against 1,000); the same swap PLUS `writesBefore = 0` leaves that floor GREEN and reds `aSECONDWindowIsNotCreditedForTheFIRSTSWrite` instead. THE GAP. The commit's own diagnosis is that these mutations hid because 'every case runs a SINGLE observe on a fresh store', and it applies the two-window fixture to `refusalsSeen` (`refusalsACCUMULATE...`) and to `released` (`aSECONDWindow...`) but not to `refusedForAnotherPod`. So the increment on line 110 can be degraded to an assignment -- turning 'how many WINDOWS were refused for another pod' into 'did any window ever' -- and MEASURED, that mutant is green across all 501 tests. Every case that reaches line 110 (`aRefusalBLAMINGANOTHERPODIsCountedAndTheReleaseIsNotCredited`, `TWORefusalsBLAMINGANOTHERPODCountTheWINDOWOnce`) runs exactly one `observe`, where 1 and 1 are indistinguishable; the sweep cannot see it because on a correct tree the counter is legitimately 0 either way, which the accessor's own javadoc at :165-175 already states. NOT BLOCKING: the row enumerated the mutations to close and all of them are closed; adding a fifth case is scope widening (AGENTS.md 'never widen scope silently'), and this is the same staleness class the row records rather than live loss. Kill, for whoever takes the row: two `observe` windows on one store and meter, each with `actingAs("podb")` inside the lambda against a partitioned `podb`, asserting `refusedForAnotherPod()` is 2. For completeness, one adjacent mutation is killed only at the sweep and not at T0/T1 -- `released++` -> `released = 1` reds `CommitProtocolSweepTest` alone and passes `aSECONDWindowIsNotCreditedForTheFIRSTSWrite`, whose 'assert 1, then assert 1' shape cannot separate an accumulator from a flag. That one IS caught, so it is recorded here rather than raised as a finding.
findings.failure_scenario: A later hand tidies `refusedForAnotherPod++` into `refusedForAnotherPod = 1` (or writes the next counter that way, reading line 110 as a boolean because the `break` directly beneath it means it can only fire once per window), runs `./gradlew :sequencer:test`, and gets 501/501 green -- MEASURED. The counter silently changes unit from windows-refused-for-another-pod to a boolean any-window-ever, which is the identical unit collapse that the `break` deletion this commit exists to kill produces in the other direction, and the sweep's `gracefulReleasesRefusedForAnotherPod` assertion cannot see it because it asserts zero.

findings.summary: Two claims in the State cell are wrong as written: the four cases are called 'T0' while testing.md's tier table and the meter's own javadoc both call cases in this file T1, and the blanket 'each was MEASURED as the SOLE killer' is false for the fourth case, as the cell's own later clause concedes.
findings.detail: TIER: the cell opens 'four T0 cases in `GracefulReleaseMeterTest`'. Every one of the four constructs `new FaultInjectingStore(new MemoryBinStore(), ...)`. testing.md's tier table puts 'backing store: none' at T0 and 'component with fakes / MemoryBinStore' at T1, so these are T1. The file's own vocabulary agrees and says so twice inside the artefact this commit edits: `GracefulReleaseMeter.java:94` ('caught only by the T1 case') and `:210-213` ('which is why the T1 case builds the situation rather than waiting for it', naming `aReleaseTheLEADERSOwnPartitionShouldHaveREFUSEDIsCounted` in this same test class). So the commit's own two artefacts disagree on the tier of the same four cases. SOLE KILLER: the cell says 'each was MEASURED as the SOLE killer of the mutation it is named for, across the sequencer module's 501 tests with the 1,000-seed sweep included', and then three sentences later says `refusalsACCUMULATEAcrossWindowsAndAreNotRECOUNTED` kills `int before = 0` and `refusalsSeen = 0` 'which the sweep also reds'. MEASURED here: both mutations red exactly two tests, that case AND `CommitProtocolSweepTest.theInvariantsHoldAcrossEverySeed`. So the opening blanket is false for one of the four and is contradicted inside its own cell. The test's own javadoc states it correctly ('killed by THIS CASE and by CommitProtocolSweepTest..., and by nothing else in the module'), which is the copy that is right. NOT BLOCKING: no test is weakened and the correct statement exists in the javadoc; this is the row cell, and review.md rule 11 applies.
findings.failure_scenario: The next hand reads the State cell to learn what this file's cases cost and where they run, believes `GracefulReleaseMeterTest` is T0 with no backing store, and either writes the next meter case against a tier contract it does not meet or reaches for `MemoryBinStore` in a genuinely T0 class on this precedent -- while `GracefulReleaseMeter.java:94` and `:210` tell them the opposite about the same four cases. Separately, a reader taking the 'SOLE killer' sentence at face value concludes the 1,000-seed sweep no longer constrains `before`/`refusalsSeen` and deletes the sweep's graceful-release accounting as redundant; measured, the sweep still reds on both.

findings.summary: The commit rewrote the comment paragraph at :96-107 and left the sentence immediately above it, at :92-95, stating a measurement this commit's own new case falsifies.
findings.detail: :92-95 reads 'COUNTED BEFORE THE CARVE-OUT, so the floor over it measures what this loop can SEE rather than what it concludes. Counting after survives the sweep and is caught only by the T1 case -- MEASURED, both ways.' MEASURED on this tree: moving `refusalsSeen++` below the carve-out block reds TWO cases -- `aRefusalBLAMINGANOTHERPODIsCountedAndTheReleaseIsNotCredited` (pre-existing) and `TWORefusalsBLAMINGANOTHERPODCountTheWINDOWOnce` (added by this commit) -- and the sweep stays GREEN. So 'survives the sweep' is still true and 'caught only by the T1 case', singular, was true before this commit and is not after it; this commit is what made it two. It is four lines above the paragraph the commit rewrote, inside the fifteen-line block whose subject is exactly this increment, and the added case's own javadoc at GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:503-508 explains why it also constrains `refusalsSeen` -- so the two statements about the same increment were written in the same commit and only one was updated. NOT BLOCKING: the sentence is not false in substance, only stale in arity, and the line is unchanged context rather than a diff line.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone auditing whether `TWORefusalsBLAMINGANOTHERPODCountTheWINDOWOnce` earns its place reads :94 -- 'counting after ... is caught only by the T1 case', singular -- takes the pre-existing `aRefusalBLAMINGANOTHERPOD...` to be that case, concludes the new one adds no falsifying power on the `refusalsSeen` side, and drops its third assertion. That assertion is what pins the truncation the narrowed `refusalsSeen()` javadoc at :155-163 now states, so the javadoc claim goes back to being unpinned prose -- which is the defect class the memory of this milestone records as dominant.
